title: Refactoring with AI
description: Use AI to safely modernize legacy code, extract functions, simplify complexity, and improve code quality without breaking things.

data.text: Why AI Is Perfect for Refactoring

Refactoring is the process of improving code structure without changing its behavior. It is tedious, error-prone, and requires deep understanding of the existing code. AI excels here because it can quickly analyze a function, identify improvement opportunities, and propose concrete changes — all while explaining the reasoning. The key is to refactor in small, testable steps.

data.title: A safe AI-assisted refactoring process:
items: Run the existing tests to establish a green baseline
Select the function or module to refactor and paste it into the AI
Describe the specific refactoring: 'Extract the validation logic into a separate validateInput function'
Review the proposed changes — ensure they preserve behavior
Apply the changes and run tests again

data.title: Tasks AI handles well:
items: Extracting functions from large, monolithic functions
Converting callbacks to async/await or promises
Replacing repetitive code with loops or higher-order functions
Replacing magic numbers with named constants
Converting class components to functional components (React)

data.text: Legacy code is often the hardest to refactor because it lacks tests and documentation. When working with legacy code, start by asking the AI to explain what the code does before asking for changes. 'Please explain what this function does step by step, then suggest three refactorings that would make it more maintainable.' Once you understand the code, proceed with small, test-backed refactorings.

data.title: Effective refactoring prompts:
items: 'Refactor this function to use async/await instead of callbacks'
'Extract the data validation into a separate Zod schema'
'Break this 100-line function into 3 smaller functions with clear responsibilities'
'Replace the switch statement with a lookup object'
'Convert this class component to a functional component using hooks'

data.title: Always run tests after refactoring
data.text: Refactoring without tests is refactoring blind. If there are no tests, ask the AI to write tests for the current behavior first, then refactor. The tests become your safety net.

Large refactorings that touch many files are best handled by agentic tools like Cursor Composer or GitHub Copilot Workspace. For IDE-based tools, break the refactoring into logical steps: extract one set of functions, run tests, then extract the next. Do not try to refactor an entire module in one go.

AI refactorings can introduce subtle bugs — the code runs but behaves differently. This happens when the AI changes variable names, reorders logic, or changes error handling while preserving the surface-level behavior. Catch these by running your full test suite and manually testing the affected features. If a test fails, paste the error back into the chat for a targeted fix.

data.title: Refactoring prompt with safety constraints
data.content: "Refactor this data processing function to separate concerns: 1) data fetching, 2) validation, 3) transformation, 4) persistence. Preserve exact behavior including error handling and logging. Do NOT change function signatures. Do NOT add new dependencies. Add unit tests for each extracted function using Jest."
data.code:
Refactoring prompt with safety:

"Refactor this data processing function to separate concerns:
1) data fetching
2) validation
3) transformation
4) persistence

Preserve exact behavior including error handling and logging. Do NOT change function signatures. Do NOT add new dependencies. Add unit tests for each extracted function using Jest."

data.text: After refactoring, measure the improvement in code quality. Common metrics: cyclomatic complexity (use a linter), function length, number of parameters, and test coverage. If the refactoring makes the code harder to test or more complex, it may not be an improvement despite feeling cleaner.

data.title: Refactoring with AI
points: Always establish a green test baseline before refactoring
Explain legacy code before changing it
Run tests after every refactoring step
Use agentic tools for large multi-file refactorings
Verify behavior is preserved, not just syntax
